page.notes:
Woodcut emblem (oval with decorative cartouche): a flaming heart or sun-burst with a hand-and-flower device at centre, an ornamental scroll frame, and a ring inscription around it. The top of the ring reads roughly "SERVATA FIDES" and the right side "HARNISCH", but the bottom and left arcs are not legible enough to transcribe reliably; the ring is given as one illegible line. A Hebrew tetragrammaton appears in a small cartouche above the emblem centre, and small letters on the ring are not legible.
Date line: printed as "M. D. XCIIX." (letters X C I I X). This is not a regular Roman numeral for 1599 (XCIX); the printed form is copied as it stands and is likely a printing error or a misreading of the scan.
Manuscript annotations in brown ink on the left and right of the emblem (fragments such as "Cap.", "5", "6", "2") are handwriting and have been left out.
Spelling was normalised for u/v and i/j as required: EIVS, NVNC, DENVO, STVDIO, HAEREDVM, PAVLO, TRACTATVS, SCRIPTVRA, NEVSTADII, PALATINATV, and IOHAN. were written as EIUS, NUNC, DENUO, STUDIO, HAEREDUM, PAULO, TRACTATUS, SCRIPTURA, NEUSTADII, PALATINATU, and JOHAN. The doubled V in "VVilhelmi" is kept as printed, since it stands for W.
